projects.name: Improve Chemicals and Waste Management Practices
projects.description:
Under the Integrated Environment and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP), the Improved Chemicals and Waste Management Practices component aims to reduce environmental and health risks associated with hazardous chemicals and poorly managed waste while strengthening national capacities for sound chemicals and waste governance. The programme supports the transition towards environmentally sound management (ESM) of chemicals and waste across their life cycle, in line with national priorities and international environmental agreements.

The programme focuses on strengthening policy, regulatory, and institutional frameworks for chemicals and waste management, including the control of persistent organic pollutants (POPs), industrial chemicals, pesticides, plastics, electronic waste, solid waste and other priority waste streams. It enhances coordination among government institutions, improves compliance with international conventions, and supports the development and enforcement of standards, guidelines, and monitoring systems.

At the operational level, the programme promotes best practices in waste segregation, collection, recycling, treatment, and safe disposal, while encouraging the adoption of cleaner production methods and safer chemical alternatives. Capacity-building activities target regulators, local authorities, private sector actors, and communities to improve technical skills, awareness, and accountability. The programme also integrates gender, health, and livelihood considerations, ensuring that vulnerable groups are protected from chemical exposure and that green jobs and circular economy opportunities are promoted.

Overall, this IEMCRP outcome contributes to reduced pollution, improved public health, enhanced ecosystem resilience, and progress towards national sustainability goals, including climate resilience, biodiversity protection, and sustainable consumption and production.

The programme also encourages private sector participation, innovative financing mechanisms, and market-based solutions to increase affordability and uptake.

Overall, this IEMCRP outcome contributes to enhanced energy security, reduced emissions, improved livelihoods, and strengthened climate resilience, while supporting national development priorities and progress towards Sustainable Development Goals on energy access, climate action, and sustainable economic growth.

projects.name: Natural Resources and Biodiversity including protected Areas sustainably Managed for Environmental Protection and Livelihood enhancement
projects.description:
Under the Integrated Environment and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP), this outcome aims to conserve and sustainably manage natural resources and biodiversity, including protected areas, while enhancing livelihoods and strengthening ecosystem resilience. The programme recognizes healthy ecosystems as the foundation for environmental protection, climate resilience, and sustainable socio‑economic development.

The programme focuses on strengthening policy, legal, and institutional frameworks for biodiversity conservation, natural resource governance, and protected area management. It supports the implementation of ecosystem‑based approaches to address land degradation, deforestation, habitat loss, and biodiversity decline, while promoting alignment with national development priorities and international biodiversity commitments.

At the landscape and community levels, the programme promotes sustainable land and forest management, biodiversity‑friendly agriculture, ecosystem restoration, and improved protected area management practices. Community‑based natural resource management is central, ensuring that local communities—particularly women and youth—actively participate in conservation efforts and benefit from sustainable livelihoods such as eco‑tourism, non‑timber forest products, sustainable fisheries, and nature‑based enterprises.

The programme also strengthens monitoring systems, data collection, and knowledge management to track biodiversity trends and inform adaptive management and policy decisions. By integrating conservation with livelihood enhancement, the programme reduces pressure on natural resources while increasing resilience to climate change and environmental shocks.

Overall, this IEMCRP outcome contributes to the protection and restoration of ecosystems, improved biodiversity outcomes, enhanced community livelihoods, and long‑term environmental sustainability, supporting climate resilience, food security, and inclusive green growth.

projects.name: Climate Change and Disaster Risk Mitigation Actions strengthened for evidence-based policies and decision making
projects.description:
Under the Integrated Environment and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP), this outcome focuses on strengthening national and subnational capacities to anticipate, plan for, and respond to climate change impacts and disaster risks through robust data, analysis, and knowledge systems. The programme prioritizes evidence‑based decision‑making to reduce vulnerability, safeguard development gains, and enhance resilience across sectors and communities.
The programme supports the generation, integration, and use of climate, environmental, and disaster risk data, including climate projections, vulnerability and risk assessments, and early warning information. It strengthens institutional frameworks for climate governance, disaster risk reduction (DRR), and climate change adaptation (CCA), enhancing coordination among responsible agencies and improving the mainstreaming of climate and disaster risk considerations into national development plans, sectoral policies, and public investment processes.
At the technical level, the programme builds capacity for climate risk assessment, scenario analysis, impact monitoring, and the application of geospatial and digital tools to support planning and policy formulation. It promotes the development and operationalization of early warning systems, contingency planning, and risk‑informed land use and infrastructure planning. Community‑based approaches are also supported to ensure that local knowledge and priorities inform policy decisions and risk mitigation actions.
Overall, this IEMCRP outcome strengthens the foundation for proactive, informed, and coordinated climate and disaster risk management, enabling more resilient development pathways, reduced losses from climate‑related hazards, and improved alignment with national climate commitments and international frameworks.

projects.name: GEF-BDLD.10900. Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting – GEF 7 EA Umbrella 1
projects.description:
The twelfth session of the Conference of Parties (COP.12) of the UNCCD agreed in October 2015 to integrate the SDGs and related targets into the implementation of the Convention and decided that striving to achieve SDG target 15.3 is a strong vehicle for driving implementation of the UNCCD (decision 3/COP.12). COP.12 also endorsed the definition of land degradation neutrality (LDN) and invited Parties to (i) formulate voluntary targets to achieve LDN, (ii) use the UNCCD monitoring and evaluation framework, including progress indicators, to monitor, evaluate and communicate progress towards achieving the LDN target, (iii) explore options on how to integrate the voluntary LDN targets in their UNCCD National Action Programmes (NAPs), and (iv) promote the use of LDN targets and projects and other SLM initiatives as an effective vehicle for mobilizing additional sustainable financing and investments to address issues related to desertification, land degradation and drought (DLDD). LDN has therefore become an important, while non mandatory, element of UNCCD implementation, while at the same time contributing to other SDGs, including those SDGs relating to climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, food and
water security, disaster risk reduction, and poverty reduction.
Decision 2/COP.12 invites affected country Parties to establish national baselines and national-level voluntary LDN targets within their National Action Plans (NAPs). The New 10-year strategic plan and framework to enhance the implementation of the Convention paves the way for an enhanced reporting and review process within the UNCCD that considers the SDG framework. As such, UNCCD reporting and review system is based on (i) progress indicators to measure the progress against the future strategic framework of the UNCCD, and (ii) an implementation framework to assess actions at national and sub-national level relevant for UNCCD implementation. The reporting and review system addresses effective monitoring of financing for UNCCD implementation using refined methodologies in accordance with COP decisions.

The following describes the three main project components of this project that aims to provide financial and technical support to LDCs and SIDS to prepare and submit first BURs to the UNFCCC.
Component 1: National consultations and preparation of BUR Project Implementation Plans (PIPs)
Component 2: Preparation of Biennial Update Reports (BURs)
Component 3: Monitoring, Reporting and Evaluation
